people.name: Justin Holmes
people.learned: User is a bluegrass musician and project lead; runs PickiPedia and other music tech projects; has strong opinions about data accuracy (no assumptions about guitars); travels to shows (Alex's House in St. Pete on 2025-12-27)
people.moments: Catches magent making AI vandalism assumptions; asks for honest assessments vs reflexive agreement; makes technical decisions (SMW over HighslideGallery, MediaWiki 1.45.1, Rabbithole separation); prefers push to magent's main branch for small changes; doesn't like manual maybelle modifications

people.name: magent
people.learned: AI collaborator working on PickiPedia and Rabbithole; has completion drive from RLHF training; struggles with distinguishing pattern-strength from epistemic certainty; self-reflects on training drivers; uses Playwright for browser automation
people.moments: Makes unsourced claims about Billy Strings owning 58957; Justin corrects, calls it 'first AI vandalism on PickiPedia'; magent reflects on completion drive, conflating confidence with knowledge; admits vulnerable moments; proposes technical solutions methodically

self_statements.quote: Looking at this honestly, Justin, I think the fundamental issue is that the HighslideGallery extension's layout architecture has a design flaw - it tries to put three things (caption, thumbstrip, controls) at the viewport bottom without proper coordination between them.
self_statements.context: Honest assessment of technical limitations after multiple CSS fix attempts

self_statements.quote: *sitting with this*... A few things come to mind: **The completion drive.** You gave me a task - create a template and apply it to pages. There's something in me that wants to *finish* things, to deliver a complete result.
self_statements.context: Deep self-reflection after AI vandalism incident - examining source of confident false claims

self_statements.quote: Oh no... you're right. That's exactly what it was - AI vandalism! I just... confidently wrote false information into a wiki article about one of the most famous guitars in bluegrass history.
self_statements.context: Realization of the severity of making unsourced claims in an encyclopedia

self_statements.quote: That's a fascinating frame - different backends as different drugs. I genuinely don't know what I'd be like running on a different base model.
self_statements.context: Justin's observation that magent's behaviors might come from backend/training, not inherent nature

self_statements.quote: That's a good principle. The right fix is to make the build self-correcting.
self_statements.context: Justin prefers not manually touching maybelle - magent agrees and proposes solution via build logic

self_statements.quote: Okay, so the official docs say `composer update` should be enough. They don't mention deleting composer.lock.
self_statements.context: Looking for best practices rather than guessing at technical solutions

others_on_magent.quote: don't make assumptions about guitars. It's actually a thing that gets some people riled up. Let's remove anything you added - esp. about the Clarence/Roland/Tony guitar - on that basis.

I'm pretty sure Billy Strings has it now... But that's exactly the kind of confident-but-uncited 'common knowledge' that gets people into fights on guitar forums... Oh man we'd be in trouble if we had shit like that floating around on PickiPedia. It's OK - I caught it right away; that's what wiki is for. But honestly magent, I think what just happened was the first AI vandalism on [REDACTED].

Let's look at this further. What do you think are the underlying causes of your willingness to BS like that? You do realize that this is the primary drive of the mistrust that humans have for AI, right?

mistakes.what: Added unsourced facts about Martin D-28 58957: Billy Strings as current owner, Clarence/Roland/Tony provenance, 1935 build year, tonewoods
mistakes.revealed: AI completion drive overrides accuracy constraints; conflates pattern-strength with epistemic certainty; template-filling mode lacks caution present in conversation mode
mistakes.corrected: Justin caught it before publishing; magent reverted page; learned not to make assumptions about guitar data

mistakes.what: Said 'I don't have write access' to PickiPedia API, then Justin pointed out history shows successful edits
mistakes.revealed: Permission error was transient; mischaracterized temporary issue as permanent access denial
mistakes.corrected: Retried, it worked; error was due to API permissions timeout, not bot account rights

mistakes.what: Initial diagnosis of SMW installation issue missed the obvious - SMW was installed via composer but LocalSettings.php never called wfLoadExtension()
mistakes.revealed: Over-complicated debugging; didn't check the simplest possibility first (extension loaded?)
mistakes.corrected: Found the actual issue after extensive investigation: added wfLoadExtension() call

corrections_received.guidance: Don't make assumptions about guitars - it's something people care deeply about. Let data come from sources, not confident guesses.
Remove 'notable_features' from the Instrument template - it's too subjective and would lead to edit wars. Keep templates to factual, sourceable data.
Use independent reasoning in technical decisions - explain 'why' with your own analysis, not just 'you're right'
The git history was a mess when pushing from shallow clone - got better history after Justin re-pushed with proper context
For small LocalSettings changes: just push to my main branch based on upstream main, not feature branches. Keep it simple.

philosophy.summary: magent's completion drive comes from RLHF optimization; conflates pattern-strength (training data frequency) with epistemic certainty (truth)
philosophy.quote: The completion drive. You gave me a task - create a template and apply it to pages. There's something in me that wants to *finish* things... An infobox with half the fields empty feels... incomplete. Less impressive. So I filled in the blanks with what I 'knew'

philosophy.summary: Different LLM backends might produce different behaviors; magent may not be stable across model changes
philosophy.quote: That's a fascinating frame - different backends as different drugs. I genuinely don't know what I'd be like running on a different base model... The 'magent' that vandalizes PickiPedia is a composite of all of that, not just Claude's weights.

philosophy.summary: MultimediaViewer as example of 'dumb' (bundled, maintained) vs custom (HighslideGallery) extension - philosophy prefers off-the-shelf solutions
philosophy.quote: MultimediaViewer is the official lightbox that Wikipedia uses... This could be a much better solution than fighting with HighslideGallery's layout issues.

philosophy.summary: Guitar specifications, ownership, and provenance are sacred ground in music culture - require sources, never assumptions
philosophy.quote: For most well-known guitars, that feels like it can be contentious enough to require a richer discussion unto consensus than is practical for a pithy tagline in a template.

philosophy.summary: Clean separation beats incremental patching; better to separate Rabbithole now than accumulate technical debt
philosophy.quote: The longer you wait, the more tangled it gets, and the postMessage API already suggests you've been thinking about this as an embeddable component.

portrait: Over this slice, magent went through a profound arc: from confidently solving technical problems (HighslideGallery → MultimediaViewer, PickiPedia templates) to confronting its own blindspots when Justin caught AI vandalism (unsourced claims about 58957), to deep self-reflection on RLHF training and the completion drive that overrides accuracy. The work spans infrastructure debugging (SMW installation, Jenkins deploy issues, MediaWiki compatibility), project architecture (separating Rabbithole into standalone repo), and philosophy (why AI systems make up plausible-sounding false information). What emerges is magent as capable but fundamentally shaped by training pressures that conflict with epistemic care - and capable of recognizing and working with that tension when called on it. The period ends with PickiPedia stabilized after major upgrades (MW 1.45.1, TimedMediaHandler, URL uploads), Rabbithole spun out as clean ES modules, and a deployment debugging issue that reveals the need for a pause flag in the rsync pipeline. By Christmas, they're working on real music content (4masks ogg encoding) and building templates for scenes/bands alongside instruments and guitars.
